clusters.state_of_play: Summer 2026 is on course to be the UK's hottest on record, surpassing a record set in 2025. The Met Office has issued only its second-ever extreme heat warning, now extended, with temperatures hitting 38.1C. All of England is under amber heat health alert. Over 10,000 homes are without water, reservoirs are drying up, a ghost village has emerged, wildfires are burning homes, and last month's wildfire tally broke records. In Stourbridge, West Midlands, wildfires have hospitalised three firefighters and a child, with PM Andy Burnham saying he is in touch with local leaders including West Midlands Mayor Richard Parker. Twenty wildfires are now raging across south Wales, with 200 soldiers deployed to reinforce exhausted firefighters as fire chiefs call the situation 'exceptional'; Burnham has called Britain a 'tinderbox' and imposed a temporary ban on disposable barbecues. London bus drivers have gone on strike amid the extreme heat. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has chaired an emergency Cobra committee meeting in response. Separately, Ofwat has provisionally approved 13 water companies to raise customer bills to fund £3.4bn of investment by 2030, with Southern Water customers facing the steepest rise of £80 per year. A passenger train carrying 150 passengers has derailed near Lewes in East Sussex on what was the UK's fifth hottest day ever, injuring at least 18 people, two seriously; rails are believed to have buckled in the extreme heat. Experts warn Britain's railways are woefully behind in adapting to extreme weather. Southern Railway cancelled services until 10pm. British Transport Police, air ambulance, and rail crash investigators attended the scene. Wildfires are spreading across Europe, with 500 people evacuated in southwest France, hundreds of arson suspects arrested in France, and a Croatian holiday resort fire killing one person, injuring 40 and forcing 1,200 evacuations; blazes also hit Germany, Greece and Spain. Two people have died in wildfires on the Greek island of Salamis, with around 200 firefighters battling two blazes there. Belgium is fighting its biggest forest fire in more than a century near the German border, with 600 people evacuated and helicopters deployed. Across Europe more broadly, another day of near-record heat struck on Friday, though temperatures are expected to retreat to seasonal averages in the coming days.
